featured_reviews.name: Sajeev Shekhar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely disappointing and unacceptable experience with MG Service Center, Malad West, Mumbai.

I own an MG Astor and my experience with this service center over the last three months has been horrendous.

My first service itself started badly. I had taken an appointment on call, but when I reached the service center, I was told there was no appointment and was made to wait for almost 1.5 hours. During the service, I was unnecessarily pressured about ceramic coating charges of around ₹36,000 despite having proof that the previous owner had already paid for it. Even though the details were apparently in their system, I was still misled.

The car was delivered more than two hours late and, shockingly, without my rear boot/dickey tray. After following up for more than a week, the tray was returned dirty, dusty, broken, and not fitting properly.

Within 10 days of servicing, my battery failed and had to be replaced. Later, my car suddenly stopped in the middle of the road while driving, which was extremely unsafe and stressful. The towing support was promised within 75 minutes, but the towing vehicle arrived almost 3 hours after the complaint and nearly 4 hours after the breakdown.

After the car was taken to the service center, there was no update for two full days. I had to keep calling and searching for numbers just to find out what was happening. I was then told they did not have enough staff to attend to the car. The repair timeline given was 10 days, but even after 14 days, there has been no proper communication.

My request for a replacement car was ignored. The service advisor has been reading my messages for days but not replying, and calls are not being answered. This is not just poor service — it is complete disregard for the customer.

MG may sell premium cars, but this service center has delivered a completely non-premium, careless, and frustrating experience.

I strongly advise MG owners to be extremely cautious before trusting this service center. The lack of communication, accountability, punctuality, and basic respect for customers is shocking.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Thank you for sharing your feedback with us. We regret that we didn’t meet your expectations, pls be rest assured, we will keep you updated and aim to resolve this promptly.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Everything about my experience with the Tata Nexon EV (2025 model) was smooth—from the initial inquiry to the delivery. However, that positivity vanished the moment I tried to actually use the car.
​The Issue:
I have spent two consecutive Saturdays (hours of my personal time) trying to get this brand-new car to charge at public fast-charging stations. To my utter frustration, the car refused to initiate a charge every single time. It is exhausting to spend your weekends troubleshooting a vehicle that should be at its peak performance.
​The Reality:
When you buy a top-of-the-line EV, you expect the freedom to travel. Instead, I am stuck with a car that has a fundamental "handshake" or hardware error right out of the gate. This isn't just a minor glitch; it’s a failure of the car's core purpose.
​My Advice to Potential Buyers:
​Think Twice: Do not assume that a smooth sales process equals a road-ready car. A new EV that cannot utilize DC fast chargers is a liability, not an asset.
​Demand a Real-World Demo: Don't settle for the home-charger demo in the showroom. Insist that the staff takes you to a public DC fast charger to verify the car actually works with third-party infrastructure before you take delivery.
